newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower despite BOK intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower despite BOK intervention.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Wednesday despite a central bank intervention as the U.S. unit's strength against the Japanese yen in global markets pressured the local unit, dealers said.
The won closed at 889.70 after opening at 889.40. It moved between 889.20 and 889.80, the lowest since the nation introduced the market average system in March 1990.

The Bank of Korea (BOK) offered to sell dollars in early morning at 917.00 won in six-month forward trading to support the won. But no contracts were made of $30 million offered by the bank, dealers said.
But the bank denied the intervention as it routinely does.
The dollar rose to 124.20/30 yen today from 123.20/30 on Tuesday, dealers said.
Dealers said trading was thin due to fears of the central bank's dollar sales intervention. The widening trade deficit was to blame for the won's weakness, they said.
A foreign bank dealer forecast a range of 888.00 and 892.00 on Thursday, while a domestic bank dealer put it between 888.00 and 890.00.
The won's mid-rate was expected to be pegged at 889.50 on Thursday, compared with 888.70 today.
